caption: AI drafts can feel convincing even when they aren’t. This carousel gives a practical five-step verification routine for AI output. Use it before you publish anything AI-generated. Do you run a source verification pass before publishing? #AI #Productivity #DecisionMaking

slides.title: MISTAKE: AI drafts
slides.body: You trust AI outputs too easily. Here are five prompts to verify work and catch hidden errors.

slides.title: 1. Diagnose claims
slides.body: Prompt: Take [DOCUMENT]. Extract all factual claims. Mark unverified items; list missing sources; produce a quick reliability score (0–100).

slides.title: 2. Improve credibility
slides.body: Prompt: For each claim with sources, rate source reliability (1-5) and suggest stronger citations; rewrite questionable sentence.

slides.title: 3. Apply checks
slides.body: Prompt: Summarize the document’s conclusions; verify against the cited evidence; if mismatch, propose corrected conclusion.

slides.title: 4. Check bias
slides.body: Prompt: Identify potential bias in framing; note omitted viewpoints; adjust tone to neutral; provide alternative interpretations.

slides.title: 5. Refine workflow
slides.body: Prompt: Generate a QA checklist for future AI outputs; include sources, cross-checks, bias notes, and a confidence meter.

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: Closing: Save this five-step verification routine for future AI outputs; follow @naelbuildingbig for more practical prompts.
